name: Right-wing dictatorship
summary: Right-wing dictatorships are authoritarian regimes, usually led by a military junta or a strongman, that justify rule as defending order, nation, tradition and property against communism and subversion. They suspend or abolish competitive politics, censor the press, and often ally with the church, while their economics range from Catholic corporatism to market liberalization.
scope: The mainstream of the interwar and Cold War conservative-authoritarian and military regimes as documented in the Wikipedia survey: Salazar's Estado Novo, Franco, Pinochet's junta (via its 1974 Declaration of Principles as quoted by the IACHR) and Brazil's AI-5 military regime, plus Park Chung Hee. It excludes fully fascist movements with mass parties (see fascism) and sits close to authoritarian conservatism; economic and religious answers are often split or low confidence because these regimes diverged.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Right-wing dictatorships split on welfare (Estado Novo was minimal, others varied), so a state guarantee is inferred as mildly disfavored.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Estado Novo kept state control over wages and aimed to prevent class struggle, so substantial pro-labor wage rises were not its policy.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Pinochet's Chile was laissez-faire while Salazar's regime was protectionist and state-steered, so adherents are genuinely split.

public-ownership.rationale: Mixed record: Estado Novo directed investment through the state and large conglomerates, while Pinochet-style regimes privatized.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Inferred from their defense of the existing social hierarchy and property order; the sources do not discuss tax rates.

unions-good.rationale: The article notes these regimes suppressed labour movements and replaced them with corporatist bodies, so independent unions are not seen as good.

property-fundamental.rationale: Anti-communist defense of the existing order includes private property, though AI-5 lets the executive confiscate assets, so not strongly.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporatist regimes regulated firms heavily while market-oriented juntas deregulated; adherents are split.

cut-welfare.rationale: Pinochet-style regimes cut welfare but Catholic corporatist regimes stressed social order; no consistent line.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Chilean Declaration is explicitly anti-Marxist and these regimes crushed worker-control movements, so collective ownership by workers is rejected.

surveillance-ok.rationale: AI-5 Art. 9 allows censorship of correspondence and telecommunications and Art. 10 suspends habeas corpus for national-security crimes.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the social conservatism and law-and-order emphasis the article lists for these regimes; drug policy itself is not discussed.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: These regimes restricted speech widely but to protect the state and order, not to protect minorities, so this specific restriction is not endorsed.

strong-leader.rationale: Authoritarian conservatism concentrates authority in a strong executive, and Schmitt's theory of dictatorial presidential power is a named intellectual root.

state-harmful.rationale: The article defines these regimes as authoritarian states upholding order, the opposite of treating the state as harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred: regimes monopolizing force tend to disarm the population, though not discussed in the sources.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Chilean junta's Declaration says the armed forces took full political power and tied their role to broad national security.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic-family emphasis of Estado Novo style regimes.

decide-locally.rationale: AI-5 Art. 3 lets the President take over states and municipalities without constitutional limits, centralizing power.

rehabilitation.rationale: Law and order is a listed characteristic; punishment is inferred to take priority over rehabilitation.

traditional-family.rationale: Estado Novo's motto was God, Fatherland and Family and its Catholic philosophy centered the family.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Authoritarian conservatism rests on traditional religion and order, so recognizing same-sex marriage is rejected.

abortion-legal.rationale: Catholic-aligned regimes upheld church doctrine on family life; non-Catholic juntas are less committed, so moderate.

more-religion-public.rationale: The article cites close church-state alliances such as Estado Novo and Austria's Federal State, though secular juntas exist.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from defense of the existing hierarchy; sources do not address racial redress.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the traditional family and Catholic doctrine of Estado Novo style regimes.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The article lists nationalism and appeals to traditionalism as core marks of right-wing dictatorships.

gradual-change.rationale: They claim to uphold the conservative status quo, but many seized power by coup, so adherents' stance is mixed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from the nationalism the article lists as a core mark; no source here discusses immigration levels.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalism and sovereignty are core marks, so ceding power to international bodies is disfavored.

free-trade.rationale: Estado Novo was protectionist while Pinochet's Chile liberalized, so adherents are split.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism is one of the core characteristics the article gives for right-wing dictatorships, so national interest outranks global cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The Declaration frames human rights as a national matter; inferred rejection of intervention on that ground.

open-borders.rationale: Order-focused nationalist regimes treat borders as part of national sovereignty, so eventual open borders is rejected on the basis of the nationalism the article lists.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred; regimes such as Park's and Pinochet's pursued rapid growth and the sources note market reforms under strong states.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic for most regimes; inferred from growth and order priorities.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Neither stated nor opposed; technocratic regimes were optimistic but traditionalists less so.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from these regimes' state-led development and national-strength goals; nuclear power is not discussed in the sources.

revolution-justified.rationale: AI-5's preamble presents the 1964 coup as a revolution that cannot be halted, though revolution from the left is rejected.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred: authoritarian regimes often put technocrats in charge and distrust mass politics.

central-planning.rationale: Anti-communism implies rejection of Soviet planning, though some regimes directed investment.

socialized-markets.rationale: The Chilean junta declared itself anti-Marxist and these regimes crushed socialist movements, so worker or public ownership as a basis for markets is rejected.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred from the property-protecting conservatism of these regimes; a land tax replacing other taxes is not discussed in the sources.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from their defense of family and social hierarchy, which favors passing wealth down; the sources do not discuss inheritance taxes.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from the order-and-duty emphasis and the corporatist idea that welfare comes through work and family; basic income is anachronistic and not discussed.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Estado Novo had a protectionist mixed economy, though Pinochet liberalized.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Estado Novo directed investment, Pinochet's regime did not, so adherents split.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Not a defining concern; corporatist ideas of small owners compete with big-capital regimes.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: A declared anti-Marxist stance, as in the Chilean Declaration, rules out the communist goal of abolishing money and wage labor.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Salazar's budget-balancing finance ministry favored sound state finance, not abolishing central institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Estado Novo's constitution created a corporatist state, and the article notes such regimes set up corporatist economies.

one-party-rule.rationale: Estado Novo had a single non-ideological party, while juntas banned all parties, so this ideology-led version is split.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Metaxas was royalist and Franco restored a monarchy, but most juntas were republican.

democracy-best.rationale: The Declaration says Chile can never again allow an ingenuous democracy, and Estado Novo was explicitly anti-parliamentarian.

direct-votes.rationale: Regimes limited elections and abolished direct presidential voting in 1959, so mass direct lawmaking is rejected.

workers-councils.rationale: A Marxist institution; the junta states Marxist movements will never be admitted to civic life.

right-to-secede.rationale: Unitary nationalist regimes treated regional separation as subversion, so a general right to secede is rejected on the basis of the nationalism the article lists.

natural-rulers.rationale: Order, hierarchy and stratification are central to authoritarian conservatism.

political-violence-never.rationale: These regimes used coups and violence, as in Operation Condor, to suppress opponents, and justified it.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred from the militarism of armed-forces-led regimes; the sources here do not state this claim directly.

separate-church-state.rationale: The article cites close church-state alliances in several of these regimes.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Estado Novo drew on Catholic social doctrine but not scripture as law, so mild disagreement.

private-courts-defense.rationale: These regimes centralize policing and defense in the executive and armed forces.

military-superiority.rationale: The armed forces held full political power and a broad national-security role in the Chilean junta.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationalism is shared with fascism but is more traditionalist; ethnic definition varies.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Estado Novo's economic model aimed explicitly to prevent class struggle, rejecting its role as history's driver.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Hierarchy and stratification are central to authoritarian conservatism per the article, so enforced equality of outcomes is rejected.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from centralized nationalism and AI-5's removal of regional authority; the sources do not discuss indigenous peoples.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Estado Novo defended its empire as part of Portugal, so reparations are inferred as rejected.

civilizational-union.rationale: These regimes were nationalist and tied to their own state; unions of nations by shared religion or civilization are not documented in the sources.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Inferred from the regimes' emphasis on duty to God, nation and family (Estado Novo's motto), which treats pure self-interest as no moral guide.

duties-before-rights.rationale: AI-5 suspends political rights and habeas corpus for order, putting national duty above rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: These regimes never addressed the moral standing of nature and adherents are indifferent, so the answer is neutral by inference.

limit-population.rationale: Catholic-aligned regimes such as Estado Novo promoted family life and large families, so active population limits are rejected by inference.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Inferred: Park, Pinochet and Salazar-era regimes pursued industrial and economic development, so calling industrial civilization a disaster is rejected.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Traditionalism and defense of the existing order favor institutional continuity over disruptive change, so deliberately speeding up disruption is disfavored by inference.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from traditionalism and religious moral views of these regimes; the sources do not discuss body modification.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic for most of these regimes; inferred from their reliance on a human strongman or military command rather than algorithms.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: AI-5 Article 9 lets the executive censor correspondence and telecommunications, so a citizen right to uncrackable communication contradicts the regime's controls.

restore-past-order.rationale: The article says these regimes justify rule as upholding a conservative status quo.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Adherents split between pragmatic technocrats and ideologically committed anti-communists, so a neutral answer fits.

direct-action.rationale: Change through coups, but the Declaration also relies on institutions; mild rejection of street direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: AI-5 uses coercive means to build an 'authentic democratic order', so means need not match ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Inferred: these regimes valued order, national development and the state, which a hunter-gatherer return would contradict.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: A Marxist goal that declared anti-Marxist regimes reject; corporatist economies instead organize labor by function.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist principle rejected by regimes such as Chile's junta, which declared itself anti-Marxist.

production-for-use.rationale: Rejects the communist aim of abolishing profit, which these anti-Marxist regimes opposed.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Estado Novo's corporatism aimed to prevent class struggle and treat employers and workers as partners, which denies that profit is exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The junta Declaration states Chile is not neutral to Marxism and will never admit Marxist parties.

collective-farming.rationale: Anti-communist regimes rejected Soviet-style collectivization; Estado Novo-type regimes upheld traditional rural property.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis that the anti-Marxist regimes reject; the article names anti-communism as central.

taxation-theft.rationale: Strong-state regimes collected taxes and rejected anarcho-capitalist and libertarian claims that the state itself is illegitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: AI-5 restricts assembly, press and political activity for order, far beyond preventing harm to others.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Estado Novo's corporatism represented groups and the family rather than only individuals.

conscription.rationale: Militarist regimes with strong armed forces generally retained conscription.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Inferred: these regimes dismissed voting as a check but also restricted dissent and movement, so neither check was endorsed.

state-as-business.rationale: Inferred: the regimes conceived of the state as an authority representing the nation, not as a firm serving customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: Regimes prized order over liberty and did not frame freedom as material means to act; inferred, as the sources do not address the concept.

media-academia-power.rationale: AI-5's preamble cites subversive acts from political and cultural sectors, hinting at distrust of cultural elites.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Some fascist-linked regimes held race theories, most conservative dictatorships did not.

organic-representation.rationale: Estado Novo's Corporative Chamber and the Chilean Declaration's intermediate bodies represent interests rather than parties.

total-state.rationale: Salazar rejected the fascist mass party-state; authoritarian conservatism is traditionalist, not totalizing.

national-rebirth.rationale: AI-5 speaks of a revolution of national ideals that must not be frustrated; rebirth framing inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Estado Novo sought to keep its existing empire rather than expand, and most military regimes were focused inward; expansion is mildly rejected.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Modern strongman regimes rule through institutions, constitutions and the army, not feudal oaths of loyalty; inferred.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom-style bondage was not a feature of these twentieth-century regimes.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Declared anti-Marxist stance rejects power-based theories of knowledge.

universal-morality.rationale: Catholic natural-law thinking behind Estado Novo implies universal moral truths.

single-common-good.rationale: Corporatism sought to prevent class struggle and subordinate group interests to one national good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: These regimes had no common position on a Jewish state, so the answer is neutral by inference.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: No common position among these regimes on diaspora return rights; neutral by inference.

revive-national-language.rationale: No common position among these regimes on reviving fallen national languages; neutral by inference.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Corporatist state-recognized bodies replaced worker control, and worker democracy within firms was resisted as Marxist.

school-vouchers.rationale: Pinochet's regime privatized education funding while other regimes kept state-run schools or church schools, so adherents split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Salazar balanced the budget and produced surpluses as finance minister, making fiscal orthodoxy a trademark of Estado Novo.

economic-freedom.rationale: Pinochet's regime held this view; others did not, and political freedom was denied.

rule-by-example.rationale: These regimes relied on decrees, censorship and punishment under laws such as AI-5, not moral example alone.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalism is core, so each nation governing itself is affirmed, though adherents deny it in the case of their own colonies.

force-without-un.rationale: Inferred from nationalist sovereignty and distrust of international bodies.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Catholic-aligned and traditionalist regimes grounded authority partly in religion and custom, not reason alone.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Inferred from the nationalism the article lists: scarce benefits go to the national community.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from the duty-and-order emphasis of these regimes; welfare conditioned on work fits corporatist logic.

class-collaboration.rationale: Estado Novo's corporatist model was designed to prevent class struggle by integrating employers and workers.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Traditionalism values inherited institutions, so sacrificing museums and libraries for novelty is rejected.

dominated-front.rationale: These regimes tended to align with Western powers against communism, so a common front against them is rejected.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism and anti-communism reject international class organization.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Estado Novo's Catholic family emphasis; women's franchise was restricted by extra requirements.

ban-interest.rationale: Interest-bearing banking continued under these regimes; a legal ban is not part of any program, though Catholic doctrine once opposed usury.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racial segregation by law is not a general feature of these regimes, so adherents mostly reject it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist thesis; anti-Marxist regimes rejected the idea that the state serves one class.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Inferred from industrial-growth priorities; energy policy is not covered by the sources.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from nationalism and the preservation of national culture that the article lists as core.

elite-replacement.rationale: A far-right conspiracy theory, not part of conservative dictatorships' doctrine.

proportional-representation.rationale: Estado Novo was anti-parliamentarian and distrusted party competition, and the Declaration excludes some parties altogether.

national-mission.rationale: Estado Novo claimed a civilizing role for its empire but most military regimes did not, so adherents split.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Traditional hierarchy and gender roles are defended by these regimes, so the claim that society systematically favors men is rejected.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: AI-5 cites a fight against corruption and promises to remove the corrupt, a recurring coup justification.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is linked to fascism, not to conservative dictatorships, and Catholic regimes opposed it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: AI-5 Article 11 excludes acts under the decree from judicial review, so legal accountability for security-force abuses is rejected.

night-watchman-state.rationale: These regimes ran strong, interventionist states, so a state limited to defense, justice and property is rejected.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not a general feature of conservative dictatorships, which rested on national rather than racial doctrine.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Hierarchy is central, though equal legal rights were not explicitly denied.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist internal debate that these anti-Marxist regimes never engaged; neutral by inference.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Estado Novo regarded its overseas territories as extensions of Portugal, so labeling settler states colonial projects is rejected.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: No common stance across these regimes on religiously separate civil laws; neutral by inference.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Catholic-allied regimes favored the church's position, but restricting conversion by law was not general; neutral by inference.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not part of these regimes' programs; mildly rejected by inference.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Church-allied regimes such as Estado Novo favored religious instruction in schools, so the ban is rejected.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine about socialist states; not applicable to these regimes.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The junta declared no time limit on its rule, so authority is not made dependent on popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protectionist, state-focused economies such as Estado Novo favored export surpluses; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Not typical of conservative dictatorships, which targeted political enemies rather than ethnic minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: AI-5 and the Declaration justify using state force against subversion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Pinochet-style market advocacy agrees but corporatist harmony rejects competition, so adherents split.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The Declaration says Marxist parties and movements will never again be admitted to civic life.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Arbitrary executive power under AI-5 is exactly what this view condemns.

separated-powers.rationale: AI-5 lets the President close Congress, legislate alone and exempts his acts from judicial review.

vanguard-party.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist theory that anti-Marxist regimes reject.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Hierarchy and order take priority over giving the poor first call on laws and institutions; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: No common position among these regimes on council home sales; neutral by inference.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Right-wing dictatorships suppressed labour movements and under Estado Novo the state controlled wages.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: These regimes took no common position on the cause of poverty; neutral by inference.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred from the nationalism and traditionalism the article lists as core.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Hierarchical regimes appointed officials by command, so lotteries are rejected.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: AI-5 suspends habeas corpus, assembly and press freedoms for national security and subversion.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State-directed economies such as Estado Novo fixed prices and wages; inferred for essentials in scarcity.

party-controls-media.rationale: AI-5 Art. 9 allows censorship of the press and telecommunications, though ownership stays private.

party-commands-army.rationale: Military dictatorships are led by the army itself, not by a party; the party in Estado Novo was non-ideological and restraining.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from nationalism; naturalization rules are not discussed in the sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Not a concern of these regimes, whose elites were not pegged to workers' wages; mildly rejected.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Estado Novo's party restrained opinion rather than binding members to programs.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Nationalism and sovereignty are core marks of these regimes, so pooling it supranationally is rejected.

head-commands-forces.rationale: AI-5 vests sweeping power in the President as head of the executive, including over legislatures.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Catholic-allied regimes favored the hierarchy but this is not their program.

clerical-rule.rationale: Churches were allied but power rested with the dictator or the military, not clerics.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Nationalism rejects revolutionary defeatism, and Marxist internationalism was the enemy.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: AI-5 allows censorship, and the preamble condemns ideologies contrary to national traditions.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The Chilean junta's Declaration states no time limit on its rule, which implies indefinite tenure.

recall-officials.rationale: Rule by decree under AI-5 lets the executive remove officials, not voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: These regimes were usually anti-communist and allied to the West, so ending alliances is rejected.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: A utopian equality scheme out of line with property-protecting regimes.

people-in-arms.rationale: Rule by professional armed forces is central, so replacing them with an armed citizenry is rejected.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Estado Novo's traditionalism idealized rural life and family; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: No common position among these regimes on reunification; neutral by inference.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: AI-5 cites cultural sectors but regimes also relied on educated technocrats.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Nationalism and traditionalism favor one's own culture as higher; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Law and order and repression of opponents, though Portugal had abolished it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Catholic and traditionalist views oppose school sex education and gender equality curricula.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religious-aligned regimes might favor it while secular juntas would not; adherents split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Catholic morality and censorship powers like AI-5's imply restrictions; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: Centralized nationalism implies a single national language in public life; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from uniform state authority over all subjects.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Order and tradition are stressed over nonconformity, so encouraging eccentric living is rejected.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from financial orthodoxy; Salazar balanced budgets and honored obligations.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: A Marxist-style thesis about neocolonialism; anti-leftist regimes reject it.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Chile's junta had the constitution drafted by an appointed commission rather than an elected assembly; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The article names Park Chung Hee's and Chinese-style strong states promoting market reforms with suppressed dissent, and Pinochet's regime.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Nationalist priorities put national interest first, so global aid duties are rejected by inference.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Positions varied by regime and are not documented in the sources; neutral by inference.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Estado Novo abolished direct presidential elections in 1959 in favor of election by the National Assembly.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from Salazar's orthodox finance and technocratic rule that insulated policy from politics.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Nationalism implies reluctance to cede claimed territory, as in Estado Novo's refusal to give up its colonies.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Catholic social doctrine behind Estado Novo ties property to social function.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anti-Marxist regimes viewed the USSR as communist and an enemy, so calling it state capitalist is rejected.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from growth and state-priority emphasis.

collective-defense.rationale: Anti-communist regimes joined Western defensive alliances; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: No common position among these regimes on annexations; neutral by inference.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Several regimes allied closely with the church rather than curbing it.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Salazar's single party was non-ideological and the ruler claimed to stand above parties.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Nationalist unitary rule and a strong military make force against secession expected.

region-keeps-system.rationale: AI-5's centralization of power over states and municipalities shows hostility to regional autonomy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Dictators in these regimes were not generally held to be divine, with rare exceptions.

flat-income-tax.rationale: These regimes had no common tax doctrine; neutral by inference.

character-from-environment.rationale: Hierarchy and traditional ideas of natural order imply innate differences; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: AI-5 puts the ruler's acts beyond judicial review, and Schmitt's state of exception sits outside normal law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed by these regimes; neutral by inference.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Estado Novo gave real power to one man rather than balancing few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Salazar was celebrated for his 'Lesson'; leader worship is common but not universal.

equal-parenting.rationale: Traditional gender roles, which Estado Novo celebrated, imply maternal primacy in custody; inferred.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist doctrine not applicable to these regimes; inferred rejection.

land-redistribution.rationale: Anti-communist defense of the property order opposes seizing large estates.

refugee-return.rationale: These regimes had no common position on refugees' right to return; neutral by inference.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: No common position among these regimes on irredentist claims; neutral by inference.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Not a program of these regimes; mildly rejected by inference.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not a program of these regimes; mildly rejected by inference.

common-currency.rationale: Sovereignty emphasis disfavors shared currencies; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nationalism favors the own state over cross-border unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Centralized nationalism denies separate self-governing institutions to minorities; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist historical materialism is rejected by anti-Marxist regimes.

ban-cartels.rationale: Corporatism organized industries into state-recognized bodies rather than breaking up concentrations; inferred rejection.

no-bailouts.rationale: These regimes had no common bailout doctrine; neutral by inference.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They overrode courts, but by executive decree rather than majority will.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Traditional gender roles contradict quotas for women in public bodies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Estado Novo's Escudo Area integrated colonies economically into a protected bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from sovereignty emphasis and distrust of international rules.

moral-incentives.rationale: Corporatism and capitalism rely on pay and property; moral incentives alone are a communist notion.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: These regimes suppressed guerrillas as subversion, so the foco theory is rejected.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Defense of hierarchy and tradition opposes abolishing titles and privileges; inferred.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Traditionalism and nationalism are core marks, so school history centered on the nation is favored.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Estado Novo justified its empire via lusotropicalism, a claim of improvement through rule.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism is central; schools teaching loyalty to flag and anthem are inferred from it.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from rejection of redress and equality of outcome.

public-money-creation.rationale: Orthodox finance, as in Salazar's treasury, retained a banking system with private credit; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Anti-Marxist regimes reject the collapse thesis; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Estado Novo clung to its empire and Lusophone influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Dependency theory is rejected by anti-leftist regimes.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis rejected by anti-Marxist regimes.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: AI-5 shows these regimes could suspend rights, so entrenched limits on government are rejected.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Defenders of empire, like Estado Novo, treated colonial boundaries as valid; inferred.

elective-rulers.rationale: Estado Novo and juntas ruled without electing the supreme ruler; inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Order and authority are incompatible with vetoes by dissenting minorities.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: These regimes treated resistance as subversion, so lawful resistance to the ruler is rejected.

parliament-supreme.rationale: AI-5 allows the President to close Congress and legislate himself, subordinating parliament.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Conventional view on animal use; inferred rather than documented.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Hierarchy tied to duty is traditional conservative thinking; inferred.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The Declaration seeks depoliticized intermediate bodies and demobilization.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not a view of these regimes, which promoted national culture rather than critique it.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Marxist/Gramscian thesis rejected by anti-Marxist regimes.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is rejected by anti-leftist regimes.

party-own-road.rationale: A debate inside the communist movement; not applicable.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

return-lost-territory.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Right-wing regimes rest on opposite foundations; inferred.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-communist adherents condemn communism but dispute the equivalence of conservative authoritarianism.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US-specific historical dispute not addressed by these regimes; neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist skepticism of gender-based policy.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Right-wing authoritarians reject liberal democracy as universally suited.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Military dictatorship is the article's main model, and the Chilean junta casts the armed forces as guardians.

paid-care-work.rationale: Family-centered Catholic model assigns unpaid care to families; inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Estado Novo's emphasis on God, Fatherland and Family; inferred filial piety.

office-by-exam.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Positions varied by regime and are not documented; neutral by inference.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Catholic family doctrine in Estado Novo opposed easy divorce.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Rule by decree and no accountability to voters.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pinochet privatized pensions but others kept state systems, so adherents split.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Communal tenure is a left-wing idea rejected by property-protecting regimes.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: AI-5 lets the executive legislate once Congress is closed, bypassing parliamentary budget approval.

single-official-language.rationale: Nationalism favors one national language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Positions varied by regime and are not documented; neutral by inference.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Rejection of equality-of-outcome reasoning in favor of hierarchy.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Traditionalist critics might agree while market regimes would not; neutral.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Operation Condor involved cross-border operations against leftists, but not insurgent arming.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: A Soviet-bloc doctrine; no position among these regimes documented.

corporate-influence.rationale: Not a regime concern; the juntas allied with business, so complaint is rejected by inference.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Regimes restricting association and press could limit foreign funding to opposition; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Catholic family policy favors larger families; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Positions varied by regime; neutral by inference.

job-guarantee.rationale: State guarantees of employment were not part of these regimes' programs; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Rejection of democratic ideals makes the claim irrelevant or rejected.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Authority demands obedience, so a denial of any duty to obey law is rejected.

non-intervention.rationale: Operation Condor involved cross-border action, but sovereignty is also valued, so adherents split.

industrial-unions.rationale: Corporatist state-run syndicates replaced free unions of any kind.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: AI-5 targets 'subversives', not an ethnic minority, so this is mostly rejected.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Family and marriage are central institutions for these regimes.

public-access-to-information.rationale: AI-5 imposes censorship and removes judicial review, which contradicts a right of access to information.

local-production.rationale: Positions varied by regime; neutral by inference.

informal-organisation.rationale: Assembly and association were restricted under AI-5 and Estado Novo.

religious-nation.rationale: Clerical alliances in Estado Novo suggest a Catholic definition of the nation; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Nationalist regimes resent tribute and ritual submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Centralization under AI-5 and unitary nationalism; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Rejects the communist principle of common ownership of production.

defeat-communism.rationale: Anti-communism is the article's central shared feature, and the Chilean Declaration says Marxist parties never again.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Positions varied by regime; neutral by inference.

religion-illusion.rationale: Anti-Marxist regimes defended religion as a pillar of order.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anti-Marxist but Catholic corporatists were wary of capitalism, so mildly positive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A Marxist feminist idea rejected by these regimes.

socialized-care.rationale: Family-based care model defended by Catholic regimes.

purge-loanwords.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

treaties-binding.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Communal self-governance is rejected by hierarchical regimes.

majority-settlement.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Estado Novo's corporatist third way agrees but Pinochet's capitalism does not, so adherents split.

historical-land-claim.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not a conservative-regime doctrine; typical adherents do not deny it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Traditional morality; inferred but not documented.

suppress-opposition.rationale: PIDE persecuted opposition under Estado Novo, and AI-5 bans political activity of those it targets.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Estado Novo's Escudo Area integrated colonies economically for the metropole.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Marxist movements and mass mobilization were banned.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Left-wing theory rejected by these regimes.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Traditionalism rejects legal recognition of gender identity.

assisted-dying.rationale: Catholic doctrine upheld by Estado Novo opposes assisted dying.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: These regimes were defined by opposition to the left; the claim is rejected.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept rejected by anti-Marxist regimes.

islam-incompatible.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Catholic social doctrine in Estado Novo; other regimes secular, so mildly positive.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed by these regimes; neutral.

social-market-economy.rationale: Positions varied by regime; neutral by inference.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Armed forces are central to these regimes.

rich-first.rationale: Market-oriented regimes accepted inequality for growth; inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Anti-communist alignment with the West, though Portugal remained neutral in WWII, so mildly rejected.

dynastic-succession.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not part of any regime program; rejected as left-leaning.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Salazar imposed austerity himself and juntas accepted lender programs; inferred.

property-franchise.rationale: Estado Novo limited women's vote by education requirement, but property tests were not general, so neutral.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An eco-feminist idea rejected by traditionalism.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept rejected by anti-Marxist regimes.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Regimes censored the press themselves and rejected this Marxist critique.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: AI-5 allows decree rule outside courts, contradicting rule only by standing laws.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: No common position among these regimes; neutral by inference.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not typical of these regimes; mildly rejected.

citizens-assembly.rationale: These regimes suspended competitive politics and judicial review, as in AI-5 and the Chilean junta, and would not hand major decisions to randomly chosen citizens.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from the regimes' alliance with the church and defence of tradition, which favours inherited doctrine over revision.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: These regimes defended property and the established social order against redistribution, so most adherents would not accept curbing large fortunes for liberty's sake; inferred from their anti-communist defence of property.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Catholic-conservative and military regimes such as Franco's and Brazil's upheld traditional morality and discipline, so open service is inferred as disfavoured; the sources do not address it.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: These regimes were anti-communist and allied with the church, so state promotion of atheism was the opposite of their policy.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: They relied on police and prisons to suppress opposition, and decrees like AI-5 expanded repressive powers rather than dismantling them.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: They excluded Marxist parties and ruled through the armed forces rather than guaranteed communal shares of power; inferred from the 1974 Chilean declaration's exclusions.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Estado Novo corporatism and Catholic social order favoured church and family welfare over an expansive state, though regimes varied; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Salazar and Pinochet set no time limit on rule and abolished competitive elections, so limiting terms of elected politicians was not their concern; inferred.

vote-delegation.rationale: Competitive politics was suspended or abolished, so citizen voting, let alone revocable delegation, ran against their model of rule from above.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The issue never arose for these regimes and adherents have no shared stance; left neutral rather than inferred.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Allied with the Catholic church, which reserved priesthood to men, these regimes upheld traditional religious office; inferred.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Estado Novo promoted a Catholic family order with the husband as head of the household.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: These regimes restricted political rights even for citizens, so extending the vote to foreigners is inferred as disfavoured.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from their defence of property and, for many, market-oriented economics; split among regimes.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from their defence of property rights; not discussed in the sources.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Such regimes typically organised youth into state-run bodies for national service, as inferred from their nationalist and order-based aims; not detailed in the sources.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; regimes varied by alliance.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Regimes differed: some hosted allied bases against communism, others stressed sovereignty.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred from their nationalism and tendency to deny or suppress accounts of state violence.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from their defence of property against communism and corporatist class collaboration.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The sources show these regimes holding power by armed force and emergency powers, with the armed forces' role central.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from their nationalism and traditionalism; national continuity is not directly discussed.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from their traditionalist, order-based and church-aligned social outlook.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from their traditional family order and hierarchy.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from their nationalism and cult of the fallen; not directly sourced.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Anti-Marxism is framed as defending Christian and national civilisation, as in the 1974 Chilean declaration of principles.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from their emphasis on territorial nation-states.

culture-before-state.rationale: Inferred: these regimes put the state and order first.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from their alliance with traditional churches and tradition.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from their defence of traditional religious authority and family order.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Regimes diverged; some promoted national economic elites, others protected minorities.

independent-unions.rationale: These regimes repressed independent labour: Salazar's Estado Novo substituted state corporatist unions and Pinochet's junta excluded Marxist organisations.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: These regimes opposed socialism outright, so the question of what counts as socialist is rejected, though they would not use the term.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Regimes diverged: some such as Pinochet's privatised services, others kept state enterprises.

second-chamber.rationale: Regimes varied, from corporatist chambers in the Estado Novo to closing legislatures under AI-5; no single position.

municipal-property.rationale: These regimes upheld private property or state authority and rejected communal ownership as a socialist idea.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Centralised authority is core to these regimes; AI-5 and the Chilean declaration concentrated power in the executive.

family-wage.rationale: Estado Novo's Catholic family order supported male-breadwinner ideals, but other regimes diverged.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Medical regulation was not a defining concern of these regimes.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Ageing research was not addressed by these regimes.

anonymous-payments.rationale: These regimes relied on secret police and surveillance, so untraceable payments beyond state control are rejected.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from surveillance, censorship and secret police as defining features; the internet is anachronistic.

person-over-state.rationale: Regimes suspended political rights and habeas corpus and subordinated individuals to national order, as AI-5 shows.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Many allied with the church and defended Catholic or traditional order, as in the Estado Novo.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Centralising regimes treated regional powers as revocable by the national executive; AI-5 let the federal government intervene in states.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by these regimes; positions varied.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The mainstream of these regimes stressed national unity over race, though some such as apartheid-era regimes differed; the audit scope excludes fascist racism.

racial-pride.rationale: Nationalist pride is common, but racial pride is not a documented position of the regimes in scope.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Regimes prized military strength and imperial ambitions (the Estado Novo held its empire), though mostly fought defensively; inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Regimes differed: some pursued irredentist unity of a people while others stressed state, religion or empire over language; the sources do not settle it.

communal-electorates.rationale: These regimes abolished or managed elections and favoured corporatist or unitary order over communal representation; inferred, with Estado Novo corporatism a partial exception.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Anti-communist regimes routinely cast opposition as foreign-directed subversion threatening the nation, as in the Chilean declaration and the Brazilian AI-5 justification; the partition claim itself is inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Most such regimes were fiscally orthodox and wary of student activism, so free tuition is mildly rejected; they varied and the sources do not discuss it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Pinochet-era and Estado Novo economics favoured growth and property over new taxes on producers; inferred, not stated in the sources.

future-generations.rationale: Traditionalist rhetoric of inheritance coexists with developmentalist priorities, and the sources do not address the question.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Estado Novo and similar regimes assigned women a family-centred role under Catholic order rather than giving women's values weight in public life.

arms-reduction.rationale: The armed forces are the regime's foundation and the Chilean declaration gives them a central national role, so cutting arms to a minimum is disfavored.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Regimes that censored the press and ran secret police are inferred to keep diplomacy confidential; the sources do not discuss treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Regimes split between corporatist state direction and market liberalization, as the scope notes, so there is no common position.

missingStatements.text: A government may strip citizens of their political rights for a fixed period without a trial.
missingStatements.rationale: AI-5 Article 4 lets the President suspend a citizen's political rights for ten years.

missingStatements.text: Courts should have no power to review the government's actions taken for national security.
missingStatements.rationale: AI-5 Article 11 excludes acts under the decree from any judicial review.

missingStatements.text: Trade unions and civic associations should stay out of party politics.
missingStatements.rationale: The Chilean Declaration calls for depoliticizing intermediate bodies, and Estado Novo's party existed to restrain rather than mobilize opinion.

notes: Regimes diverged sharply: Pinochet's Chile was market-liberal, Salazar's Portugal corporatist and protectionist, Park's Korea state-led. Fascist regimes are excluded here. Several economic answers are therefore split or low confidence. Close to authoritarian-conservatism, so distinguishability may matter.
